title: Estimating the whole-body effective dose and health risks as well as introducing a new easy method for eye lens dosimetry in interventional cardiology procedures
author: Hatami, Bagheri, et al.
materials: In the new proposed method, since almost all the staff in the assessed centers used mask during their work, our new protocol for eye lens dosimetry consists of attaching two TLDs to the top border of the respiratory/surgical mask below the eye region, as illustrated in Fig. 1. The mask displacement from the initial position was recorded for all participants at the end of IC procedure (by marking the positions on participants’ skin) to evaluate the effect of TLD displacement in eye lens measurement. Furthermore, eye lens dose values obtained from the proposed protocol were compared with the values resulting from the common method. It must be mentioned that our new TLD dosimetry method was just assessed on participants who did not wear radioprotective (RP) glasses.Fig. 1Positions of TLDs attached on the top border of respiratory/surgical mask below the eye region as our new protocol for eye lens dose measurement in comparison with TLD positioned near eyes as common method.Fig 1

The annual eye lens dose for two groups (with and without RP glasses) were compared using independent t-test statistical analysis (SPSS 16, IBM, USA). Furthermore, in participants without eye RP glasses, a comparison was carried out between the eye lens dose values of the common method and our new proposed method, using a paired t-test. The resulting P-values lower than 0.05 waere considered as statistically significant differences.

The statistical analysis for TLD eye lens dosimetry comparing the common and our new method showed no significant differences using paired t-test (p-value = 0.03). Fig. 2 represents the relationship between the different displacement of TLDs on surgical masks and the percentage of dose change. The eye dose values did not differ significantly from common TLD measurements (mean difference < 4%, maximum difference < 7%) at different displacement measurements. Therefore, it can be concluded that mask movement in IC procedures had not affected the eye lens dose measurement, significantly. steps.title: Recruit study participants
steps.instruction: Enroll 160 individuals (80 physicians and 80 other staff such as nurses, radiology technologists, anesthesia technologists, and other health professionals) from eight general hospitals in Tehran, Iran, during the period July to October 2019.

steps.title: Ensure standard protective apparel
steps.instruction: Have each participant wear their usual protective lead apron throughout the interventional cardiology (IC) procedures.

steps.title: Prepare TLDs for dosimetry
steps.instruction: Obtain thermoluminescent dosimeters (TLDs) to be used for eye‑lens and whole‑body dose measurements.

steps.title: Attach TLDs – common eye‑lens method
steps.instruction: Place four TLDs near the outer side of the eyes (two on the left side and two on the right side) using TLD holders that are fixed with tape around the head.

steps.title: Attach TLDs – new mask method
steps.instruction: Attach two TLDs to the top border of a respiratory/surgical mask, positioning each TLD directly below the left and right eye regions.

steps.title: Place whole‑body TLDs
steps.instruction: According to NCRP Report 122, position one TLD on the top surface of the lead apron and a second TLD under the apron on the chest region for whole‑body dosimetry (applies to both eye‑lens methods).

steps.title: Perform IC procedure
steps.instruction: Carry out the interventional cardiology procedure while the participant wears the mask with attached TLDs (new method) or the taped head‑mounted TLD holders (common method) together with the lead apron.

steps.title: Record mask displacement
steps.instruction: At the end of the procedure, mark the positions of the TLDs on the participant’s skin to document any displacement of the mask.

steps.title: Collect TLDs for read‑out
steps.instruction: Remove all TLDs (eye‑lens and whole‑body) and send them for dose read‑out and subsequent analysis.

steps.title: Apply new method only without RP glasses
steps.instruction: Restrict the new mask‑based eye‑lens dosimetry to participants who are not wearing radioprotective (RP) glasses during the IC procedure.
